post.originalText:
every textbook draws the hydrogen atom as a fuzzy ball sitting perfectly still.

the ball is right. the "still" part isn't. even in the ground state, the calmest an atom can ever be, something inside that cloud keeps flowing, and this video shows exactly where it goes, orbital by orbital, in colors your textbook never printed.

i asked Claude to stop drawing the cartoon and render the actual math. Opus 5.5 built me the whole simulation.

ok ok ok how to read it:

the little circle in the corner is the orbital you memorized in school
the big cloud is the probability current, where the "chance of finding the electron" flows
orange: counterclockwise
blue: clockwise
white: almost still

1s, 2p, 3d. three orbitals. zero of them sitting still.

wait.

in plain Schrödinger, the 1s wave function is real, so its current is exactly zero. that's your static ball.

add spin with the Pauli equation and a new term shows up. spin ALONE makes the probability circulate. same density, same cloud, but now it's turning on the inside.

like a lake that looks frozen from the shore while the water underneath keeps moving.

and watch 3d. orange and blue in the same orbital. the orbital motion pulls one way, the spin pulls the other.

honest part, because physics twitter will come for me: the electron is NOT orbiting like a tiny planet. nothing flies around a track. what flows is probability. and the textbook isn't lying, it shows you the density and skips the current.

that current is how the math writes the atom's magnetism.

the textbook gave you a photo. the equation was always a video.
